chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: McKinney's Cotton Pickers arrive; Royal joins Les Hite at Sebastian's
summary: Royal admires McKinney's Cotton Pickers under Don Redman, and Les Hite, needing another saxophonist, calls him down from San Francisco, reuniting him with Lawrence Brown.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Oh, I worked with them about a year or so. Then a band by the name of McKinney's Cotton Pickers came to town and they went to work at Sebastian's Cotton Club. By far, they had one of the best bands that I had ever heard in my life. I think of all the bands at that time, there were only two that I really appreciated and that was Duke Ellington and McKinney's Cotton Pickers. Up to that time, that's the only bands that I could actually look up to and see that it was putting something down that was just extra special.
This band, McKinney's Cotton Pickers, at that time

was led by Don Redman and they came to work for a short time, possibly, oh, six weeks or so at Sebastian's Cotton Club in Culver City (PHONETIC), which was the biggest nightclub in the world. It seated something like 1750 people for dinner with three dance floors in it.

I was working with Curtis Moseby at the time up in San Francisco at the Apex Number Two. So, when McKinney's Cotton Pickers came out, they had four saxaphones in the band and in the early days when you had three saxaphones, that's a whole lot of saxaphones. So, these guys came out and had four saxaphones in the band and a wonderful arranger by a name of Don Redman. He had those saxaphones sounding so good that Les Hite's band, who was the house band there and followed them back in when they left, they had to try to come up to par with actually what was happening in sounds of the McKinney's Cotton Picker Band, so they needed another saxaphone player.

So, they called the kid up in San Francisco, who was me, and I came down and joined them. That's when I started working again with Lawrence. He was in that band at the time. He had left the number two band of Curtis Moseby up in San Francisco and had come to work with Les Hite at the time, so we started another allegiance and alliance with each other.
